blurb: Small bearded German ratter with a wiry coat and a watchful, spirited nature
description: The Miniature Schnauzer is a small German dog with a wiry double coat, bushy beard and eyebrows, described as alert, spirited, friendly and easy to train.
answer: The Miniature Schnauzer is a small German dog of Schnauzer type, developed in the late nineteenth century as a farm ratter. It stands 30–35 cm and weighs 4–8 kg, and the AKC standard describes it as alert, spirited, friendly and willing to please.

body: Schnauzers and Pinschers share a common history in southern Germany, where rough- and smooth-haired dogs were kept as carriage and stable dogs and ratters. The Miniature may have been developed from the smallest Standard Schnauzers or from crosses with smaller breeds such as the Affenpinscher, Miniature Pinscher and Poodle.

The rough-haired Pinscher was officially renamed Schnauzer in 1917. The FCI definitively accepted the Miniature Schnauzer in 1955, and it was listed tenth among the most-registered breeds worldwide in a 2013 FCI census. The first dogs reached the United States in 1924.

Under the international standard both sexes stand 30–35 cm and weigh 4–8 kg, with a roughly square outline. The double coat is wiry over a soft undercoat. The rectangular head carries a bushy beard, mustache and eyebrows, with dark oval eyes and V-shaped folding ears. The FCI recognises black, pepper and salt, black and silver, and white; the AKC and Canadian Kennel Club do not accept white in the show ring.

The AKC standard describes the breed as alert and spirited yet obedient, friendly, intelligent and willing to please, never overaggressive or timid. It is usually easy to train and a keen watchdog, more inclined to bark than bite, and often aloof with strangers until they are welcomed. It is described as more laid-back and less dog-aggressive than British terriers.

In show trim the coat is kept short on the body while the furnishings on the ears, legs, belly and face are retained, so regular trimming is part of ownership. Sources give little detail on exercise needs.

A UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years. Conditions reported in the breed include gall bladder mucoceles, congenital portosystemic shunts, von Willebrand disease, atopic dermatitis and Schnauzer comedo syndrome, a skin condition found only in this breed.

faq.q: How big does a Miniature Schnauzer get?
faq.a: The international standard gives a height of 30–35 cm and a weight of 4–8 kg, most often 4.5–7 kg.

faq.q: Are Miniature Schnauzers easy to train?
faq.a: They are usually described as easy to train, and Stanley Coren ranked them 12th of 140 breeds for working and obedience intelligence.

faq.q: How long do Miniature Schnauzers live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 13.3 years, and a Japanese study found 13.4 years.
